title: introduce-multi-sdk-auth-stream-synchronizer-and-ergonomic-retry-alignment
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: multiple SDKs drifted in how they schedule reauth, retry backoff baselines, and streaming resume hints. That divergence caused intermittent parity bugs (different retry windows, mismatched heartbeat behavior) and made cross-language integrations harder to reason about. This PR introduces a lightweight 'auth-stream synchronizer' concept implemented idiomatically in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to: 1) align credential refresh windows and heartbeat signals, 2) surface a small, opt-in RetryProfile shim for ergonomic defaults, and 3) add parity helpers for streaming consumers (FlowControl hints and resume token stability).

What this changes (high level):
- SDK surface: add AuthSynchronizer abstraction in each SDK (python: AuthSynchronizer, ts: authSynchronizer, go: AuthSync) that coordinates TTL-based prefetch, heartbeat jitter, and a small set of telemetry tags. Default is enabled for new sessions but opt-out via client config.
- Retry ergonomics: introduce RetryProfile presets (conservative / balanced / aggressive) and a small adapter that maps SDK-level retries to a consistent backoff baseline used by the platform. This reduces cross-sdk behavioral gaps without forcing a single policy.
- Streaming parity: streaming iterators now accept resume-hint metadata and FlowControl hinting (buffer target / soft max). Implementations add light-weight guards to avoid double-retries across reconnects.
- Telemetry: add cred.sync.v1 tags and emit a single-stanza diagnostic when a synchronizer makes a proactive refresh. Adds opt-in telemetry to reduce noisiness.
- Version bumps: python -> 2.14.0, typescript -> 1.28.0, go -> 1.8.1 (minor/patch alignment).

Checklist:
- [x] Add cross-sdk interface and local adapters
- [x] Implement tests for prefetch timing and retry baseline mapping
- [x] Add streaming resume-hint tests and integration harness for reconnects
- [x] Docs: SDK changelogs and short how-to note in /docs/sdks/auth-sync.md
- [x] Bump versions and changelogs per SDK

Commits summary: squash of incremental changes: commit 1: add core synchronizer API and interfaces across three SDKs; commit 2: implement TTL prefetch and heartbeat jitter; commit 3: add RetryProfile presets and mapping layer; commit 4: streaming resume-hint and flowcontrol integration tests; commit 5: docs and changelog updates; commit 6: tests flake fixes and CI config tweaks.

review_comments: Ava Martinez (2026-01-20): Can we document the default TTL prefetch window? Suggest defaulting to 30s before expiry for 'balanced' profile and exposing the value in constructor.

Priya Nair (2026-01-21): Responded: Default changed to 30s for balanced, added constructor option `prefetch_window` and docs note. Also added unit tests covering edge case when credential TTL < prefetch_window.
Liam O'Connell (2026-01-24): Noted a potential race between heartbeat jitter and stream reconnect. Suggested adding a small mutex in go sync implementation to avoid double-refresh.
Priya Nair (2026-01-25): Added mutex in go implementation and added a comment with rationale. Added test that simulates parallel reconnect + heartbeat.
files_reviewed_highlights: python: synchronizer has minimal external surface (start/stop/attach_session) and documented opt-out
ts: types are exported with light runtime checks to preserve ergonomics for JS consumers
go: minimal API (NewAuthSync) and thread-safe by default
docs: how-to includes migration notes for teams that previously used per-request prefetch

Increased integration timeout for stream harness to 45s to avoid CI flakiness
release_notes: Python 2.14.0: Add AuthSynchronizer and RetryProfile presets; Typescript 1.28.0: add authSynchronizer and flowcontrol hints; Go 1.8.1: add AuthSync and retry presets. Improved parity across SDKs for credential refresh timing, streaming resume hints, and retry baseline behavior. NOTE: default behavior is opt-in for existing clients (no breaking changes).
how_to_migrate: Existing clients that want prior behavior can set client.config.auth_synchronizer.enabled = false or pass `enable_synchronizer: false` when constructing clients. For teams that want stable cross-sdk retry behavior, opt into RetryProfile 'balanced' to get the default alignment. See docs/sdks/auth-sync.md for examples.
manual_backport_notes: Backport to release/2026-01 only if the customer requests aligned SDK behavior; ensure changelog callout and verify CI matrix with older runtime versions.
notes_for_release_manager: This PR touches all three SDKs and CI matrix. Coordinate staged rollout: publish python wheel and npm package, then go module tag. Monitor cred.sync.v1 telemetry and health dashboard for first 72h after release.
post_merge_actions: monitor telemetry filter cred.sync.v1 for error spikes
additional_context: This PR intentionally keeps the synchronizer opt-in for existing clients to avoid surprises; design discussions referenced ENG-4821 and included prototypes in internal dogfooding. The synchronizer is lightweight (no network calls by itself) and relies on existing credential providers to perform refreshes.
